records.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\ln(x^2)\) for \(x>0\), and let \(g(x)=e^{2x}\) for \(x>0\). Define \(H=f\circ g\) and \(K=g\circ f\).

partsPatches.label: (a)
partsPatches.answer:
Because \(g\) is defined for \(x>0\) and always has positive output,
\[
H(x)=\ln igl((e^{2x})^2 igr)=\ln(e^{4x})=4x.
\]
Thus
\[
 oxed{\operatorname{Dom}(H)=(0,\infty),\qquad H(x)=4x}.
\]

partsPatches.label: (b)
partsPatches.answer:
For \(K(x)=g(f(x))\), the input to \(g\) must be strictly positive:
\[
\ln(x^2)>0\Longleftrightarrow x^2>1.
\]
Together with the original restriction \(x>0\), this gives \(x>1\). Also
\[
K(x)=e^{2\ln(x^2)}=x^4.
\]
Therefore
\[
 oxed{\operatorname{Dom}(K)=(1,\infty),\qquad K(x)=x^4}.
\]

partsPatches.label: (d)
partsPatches.prompt: Write an expression for the position \(s\), in terms of time \(t\), if \(s=0\) when \(t=0\).

partsPatches.label: (c)
partsPatches.prompt: Give the coordinates of a point that is on the graph of \(f\) but is not on the tangent line \(\ell\).
partsPatches.answer: The point \(\boxed{(-2,-2)}\) is on the graph of \(f\) by the given information. The tangent line is \(y=x/2\), and at \(x=-2\) that line has \(y=-1\), not \(-2\). Therefore \((-2,-2)\) is not on \(\ell\).

rubric.description: 1 point for showing that the point is not on \(y=x/2\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for showing that the point is not on \(y=x/2\).

partsPatches.label: (d)
partsPatches.prompt: Give the coordinates of a point that is on the tangent line \(\ell\) but is not on the graph of \(f\).
partsPatches.answer: The point \(\boxed{(-2,-1)}\) lies on \(y=x/2\). Although it satisfies the full implicit algebraic relation, the selected continuous function has the given value \(f(-2)=-2\), so \((-2,-1)\) is not on the graph of \(f\).

rubric.description: 1 point for a valid point on the tangent line, such as \((-2,-1)\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for a valid point on the tangent line, such as \((-2,-1)\).

rubric.description: 1 point for using the selected function value \(f(-2)=-2\) to show that it is not on the graph.
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for using the selected function value \(f(-2)=-2\) to show that it is not on the graph.

partsPatches.label: (b)
partsPatches.prompt: Find the values of \(p\) and \(q\) for which \(f'\) is continuous at \(x=1\).
partsPatches.answer:
For \(f'\) to exist and be continuous at the join, \(f\) must first be continuous, so \(p+q=1\). The one-sided derivative values are \(2p\) and \(q\), so continuity of \(f'\) requires \(q=2p\). Solving
\[
p+q=1,\qquad q=2p
\]
gives
\[
 oxed{p= rac13,\qquad q= rac23}.
\]

rubric.description: 1 point for using \(p+q=1\) from continuity of \(f\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for using \(p+q=1\) from continuity of \(f\).

rubric.description: 1 point for the left derivative value \(2p\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for the left derivative value \(2p\).

rubric.description: 1 point for the right derivative value \(q\) and equation \(q=2p\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for the right derivative value \(q\) and equation \(q=2p\).
